chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

I was with him one day when a pair of wood pigeons landed on the wall and cooed their cooing. So Abu Ja'far عليه السلام responded to them in their speech for a while. Then they rose, and when they flew onto the wall, the male cooed to the female for a while, then they flew off.

So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, what is this bird?' He said, 'O Ibn Muslim, everything Allah has created among birds, beasts, or anything possessing a spirit is more hearing toward us and more obedient than the son of Adam. This wood pigeon had become suspicious of his mate, so she swore to him, "I did not do it." Then she said, "Will you accept Muhammad ibn Ali as arbiter?" So they both accepted me, and I informed him that he was being unjust to her, so he believed her.'

key_terms.ابْنِ آدَمَ: the human being, contrasted here with other living creatures
key_terms.وَرْشَانٍ: a wood pigeon whose interaction is described in the report

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the Imam's knowledge of the speech of animals?
ai.summary: This narration describes Abu Ja'far عليه السلام responding to the speech of a pair of birds and then explaining their dispute. It highlights the special knowledge and authority granted to the Imam عليه السلام, and portrays the rest of creation as more responsive and obedient to divine authority than many human beings.
